clue.text: The end of class? Hardly!

parts.note: read literally it suggests the bell at the close of a lesson, but it means the place where young ladies were polished off socially, hardly an ordinary class

explanation.surface: A pupil wonders whether the lesson is ending, and is told it most certainly is not.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue plays on two senses: finishing as ending, and a school that 'finishes' a girl's education in manners and social graces.
explanation.definitionFit: A private college teaching etiquette to young women completes, or polishes off, their upbringing, so it is the 'end' of their schooling.

clue.text: Silly ducks on lake eaten by carp, perhaps

indicators.note: eaten by means the fish swallows the other pieces, placing them inside its letters

parts.note: a carp is an example of a fish
a duck is a zero score, shaped like the letter O, so two ducks give OO
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: Birds on a pond being swallowed by a big fish seems a daft scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' marks carp as one example of the category FISH; OO and L go inside it after the F.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe someone lacking sense, so they are straightforward synonyms.

clue.text: Wants to hear about massages

indicators.note: to hear signals a word that sounds like the following one when said out loud

parts.note: to massage dough or muscles is to knead it, so massages is kneads

explanation.surface: Someone asks to be told about the treatments a spa offers.
explanation.walkthrough: KNEADS and NEEDS are pronounced the same, since the K is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: If one wants something one requires it, so the verbs are synonyms.

clue.text: Leaves with possibly 72 hours of fondly-remembered youth!

parts.note: a salad is a dish of leaves such as lettuce
72 hours is three days, one example of a number of days

explanation.surface: Lettuce and a long weekend evoke nostalgic memories of being young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' signals that 72 hours is just one way of making up some DAYS.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase comes from Shakespeare's Cleopatra recalling her green, inexperienced past, and now means one's carefree early years.

clue.text: Beg for legislation rumoured to support single member

indicators.note: in a down answer the supporting piece sits underneath, so it comes after the other pieces

parts.note: single means one, written as the Roman numeral I
MP is a Member of Parliament

indicators.note: rumoured signals a word heard, so a sound-alike is wanted

parts.note: legislation is law, which in British speech sounds like lore

explanation.surface: A lobbyist pleads for a bill that gossip says will back a lone politician.
explanation.walkthrough: In a non-rhotic British accent LAW and LORE sound the same; LORE goes beneath I and MP in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To plead earnestly is to beseech, the same as begging.

clue.text: Germany cover schedule and sparkle

indicators.note: cover means the outer piece wraps around the other, enclosing it

parts.note: a schedule is a list

explanation.surface: Germany draws up a protective timetable and dazzles.
explanation.walkthrough: GER is split around LIST: G, then LIST, then ER.
explanation.definitionFit: An old poetic word, as in 'all that glisters is not gold', meaning to glitter or shine.

clue.text: Archer is at university, protected by police

indicators.note: protected by means the second piece is guarded inside the first

parts.note: CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes police
being up means being in residence at a university

explanation.surface: A bowman studying at college is guarded by officers.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage one goes 'up' to university, so UP means at university.
explanation.definitionFit: The Roman god of love is pictured with a bow, shooting arrows of desire.

clue.text: Two ducks? Definitely!

explanation.surface: A batsman out twice for nothing is told so in no uncertain terms.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a duck is a score of nothing when the batsman is out, so two ducks are two dismissals.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket a batsman dismissed in both innings is dismissed twice over, and the phrase also means thoroughly or utterly.

clue.text: Supple smile — so different!

indicators.note: different asks for the letters to be made into something else

explanation.surface: A grin and a 'so' combine into a new, more flexible look.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' rearranges SMILE and SO together.
explanation.definitionFit: Both describe a body that bends easily and gracefully, so they are synonyms.

clue.text: Drink too much, but find common ground!

parts.note: over means excessively, as in overdone
to lap is to drink, as a cat does

explanation.surface: Someone overdoes the booze, yet still reaches agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces are taken in answer order: 'too much' comes first, then 'Drink'.
explanation.definitionFit: Two things sharing part of their area or interests coincide in part, which is what 'common ground' describes.

clue.text: I am, darling, American — the driving force!

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
pet is an endearment like darling
US stands for United States, so American

explanation.surface: A Yank introduces themselves affectionately as the power behind things.
explanation.definitionFit: Momentum or the thrust that propels something forward is its driving force.

clue.text: Imprisoned, then free, in a total reversal

parts.note: a prisoner is said to be inside
someone released is out

explanation.surface: A convict jailed and then released has had their life turned upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: A garment worn with its lining showing is turned completely the wrong way, so a total reversal.

clue.text: Most have supper and leave the dog

indicators.note: most of a word means all but its last letter

parts.note: to have supper is to dine
to leave is to go

explanation.surface: Most people eat their evening meal and then depart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Most' takes the last letter off DINE, giving DIN.
explanation.definitionFit: The wild dog of Australia, so a specific kind of dog.

clue.text: The care needed to work this land

indicators.note: to work means the letters are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Tending a field needs attention and effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'needed' is a link; 'to work' rearranges THE CARE.
explanation.definitionFit: A metric unit of area, ten thousand square metres, used to measure a plot of land.

clue.text: Authorization given to proceed if there's headroom

explanation.surface: Permission to go ahead is granted provided there is enough height.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is official permission, as for a plane to take off, and also the space between a vehicle's top and an overhead bridge.

clue.text: Fix engineers' depot

parts.note: RE are the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
a depot is a store

explanation.surface: Repair the army technicians' warehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: To repair or renovate something brings it back to working order.

clue.text: It's more frightening if taken for a gardening tool

indicators.note: taken means the outer word takes in the other piece

parts.note: scarier means more frightening

explanation.surface: Something seems even more alarming when mistaken for a garden implement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taken' puts IF inside SCARIER, after SCAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A rake-like device used to cut and loosen soil or lawn thatch.

clue.text: Implement silent reforms after mid-January

indicators.note: after places the anagram after the U

parts.note: the middle letter of January is U

indicators.note: reforms means the letters are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: A government introduces quiet changes after the middle of the new year.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges SILENT to TENSIL, which goes after U.
explanation.definitionFit: A tool or kitchen device is an implement.

clue.text: Loosen the grip of the peacekeepers?

parts.note: the UN sends peacekeeping forces
a clasp is a grip

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether the peacekeepers' hold should be relaxed.
explanation.definitionFit: To undo a fastening or release one's hold is to loosen it.

clue.text: Left university doctor having a turn — back pain?

parts.note: MB is Bachelor of Medicine, a doctor's degree
a turn, as in a game, is a go

explanation.surface: A doctor who has quit the university takes a go: is it back pain?
explanation.definitionFit: A common ache in the lower back, so a back pain.

clue.text: Loud harangue, sick at heart, and showing panic

parts.note: F is forte, musical notation for loud
a harangue is a rant

indicators.note: at heart means the middle letters of the word are used

explanation.surface: A loud tirade, sick to the core, reveals someone in alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: Being wild with worry or fear is the same as panicking.

clue.text: Scanty cover, but growth

explanation.surface: A skimpy covering might also be something that grows.
explanation.definitionFit: The fig-tree leaf traditionally covering nudity in art is a token covering, and it is literally a growth on a fig tree.

clue.text: Student in weird séance needs to wash!

indicators.note: in means the student letter goes within the other letters
weird means the letters are arranged strangely

parts.note: L is a learner, as on a learner driver's plate

explanation.surface: A learner at an odd spiritualist sitting needs a bath.
explanation.walkthrough: 'weird' rearranges SEANCE to CEANSE, and 'in' puts L inside it after the C.
explanation.definitionFit: To clean thoroughly is to wash.

clue.text: Dog no-one backed was something unusual

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: backed means turned backwards

parts.note: no gives O, a zero, and one gives I, the Roman numeral

explanation.surface: A dog nobody supported was quite a strange creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns OI into IO.
explanation.definitionFit: A curiosity or odd collectable object is an unusual item.

clue.text: When one's supporting the job centre, it's a haven

indicators.note: in a down answer supporting pieces sit below, so they follow
the centre of the word job is its middle letter

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
one's is one is, read as I plus 's, so IS

explanation.surface: A job centre propped up by someone is a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry AS and IS sit below O, the middle of 'job'.
explanation.definitionFit: A fertile spot in a desert, figuratively any refuge or haven.

clue.text: The importance found in team dug-out?

indicators.note: out signals that the letters are put out of order

explanation.surface: Is significance discovered in the sunken team shelter beside the pitch?
explanation.walkthrough: 'found' is a link; IN, TEAM and DUG are rearranged by 'out', the end of 'dug-out', a pitchside shelter.
explanation.definitionFit: Size or significance of something is its importance.

clue.text: A French individual working at marriage

parts.note: un is French for a
I is one, an individual
on means working, as a machine is on

explanation.surface: A Frenchman works hard at his marriage.
explanation.definitionFit: A wedding unites two people, so it is a union.

clue.text: Forgetting that the continent welcomes fighting men

indicators.note: welcomes means the continent takes the other piece inside

parts.note: Asia is a continent

indicators.note: fighting means the letters are scrapping and out of order

explanation.surface: Asia receives soldiers but forgets them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fighting' rearranges MEN to MNE, which goes after the first A of ASIA.
explanation.definitionFit: A loss of memory is the state of forgetting.

clue.text: Treason — the leader goes missing, and that's the issue

indicators.note: the leader is the first letter, which disappears

parts.note: sedition is incitement against the state, close to treason

explanation.surface: Treachery whose ringleader vanishes becomes the matter in question.
explanation.walkthrough: SEDITION loses its first letter S.
explanation.definitionFit: A version of a newspaper or book printed at one time is an issue.

clue.text: Encourage talks with journalists?

parts.note: to press is to urge or encourage
talks are a conference

explanation.surface: Someone urges negotiations to be held with reporters.
explanation.walkthrough: 'talks' does double duty in the surface: it supplies CONFERENCE and starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A meeting at which reporters question a speaker is a briefing with journalists.
